title: Response contracts and dependency overrides
summary: Use response_model and HTTPException, then replace a dependency in tests.

scenario.briefing: The item API now exposes internal notes and the test suite hits the real data store. Tighten the public response and make the test deterministic with a dependency override.

misconceptions.description: Leaving a dependency override installed after a test.
misconceptions.testDescription: The override is cleared after each test.
misconceptions.feedback: The override is global to the app object. Clear it in finally so later tests do not silently use fake data.

misconceptions.description: Letting the test call the real data store.
misconceptions.testDescription: The override supplies fake records instead of the real store.
misconceptions.feedback: A unit test should replace the dependency and assert the contract without external state.

misconceptions.description: Calling a blocking database client from an async endpoint.
misconceptions.diagnostic: Approving the async endpoint that runs a synchronous ORM query.
misconceptions.feedback: The event loop cannot serve other requests while the call blocks. Use def or an async driver.

sections.title: Response models define the public shape
sections.body: `@app.get("/items", response_model=list[ItemOut])` serializes only the fields declared on `ItemOut`, even when the handler returns a richer object. `HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Item not found")` turns a missing record into a documented error response instead of a server error.

sections.title: Dependencies are resolved per request
sections.body: `Depends(get_items)` tells FastAPI to call the dependency and pass its result. A test can replace it with `app.dependency_overrides[get_items] = fake_items`, call the app through `TestClient`, and clear the override in `finally` so other tests see the real dependency.

sections.title: Async handlers must not block
sections.body: An `async def` endpoint runs on the event loop. A synchronous database call such as `session.query(...).all()` blocks every other request on that worker. Use a regular `def` handler, which FastAPI runs in a thread pool, or an async driver.

steps.title: Override a dependency in a test
steps.prompt: Edit test_main.py. Override get_items so the test never reads the real store, assert that GET /items hides internal_note, and check that a missing item returns 404. Run the checks when done.

files.content:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from main import app


def test_list_items_hides_internal_fields() -> None:
    client = TestClient(app)
    # TODO: override get_items and assert the public response
    response = client.get("/items")
    assert response.status_code == 200


def test_missing_item_returns_404() -> None:
    client = TestClient(app)
    response = client.get("/items/99")
    assert response.status_code == 200

artifact.title: main.py
artifact.caption: The endpoint returns ORM objects and runs a blocking query inside an async handler.
artifact.content:
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from database import get_session
from models import Item

app = FastAPI()


@app.get("/items")
async def list_items(session: Session = Depends(get_session)) -> list[Item]:
    items = session.query(Item).all()
    return items

findings.label: The endpoint returns ORM objects without a response model.
The async endpoint runs a blocking database call.
The endpoint limits the response to explicit public fields.
The endpoint handles a missing record with a 404 response.

verdicts.label: Block the change until the response contract and database call are fixed.
Ship it; FastAPI serializes ORM objects safely.

steps.explanation: Without a response model FastAPI has no field list, so ORM columns leak and serialization can fail. The synchronous query also blocks the event loop. Return a DTO with response_model, use a sync handler or async driver, and raise HTTPException for missing rows.
hints: Check each finding against the endpoint code.
ORM objects without a response model expose every column.
A blocking query inside async def holds the event loop.
A missing 404 and an explicit response model are separate issues.
